Official 2017–2019 OUR/IM student activities: Mental fraction quotients; comparing fractional running rates; fitting a scaled drawing. Students must Compare rates in hours and fractional distances, then justify a proportional scaled sketch. First-party illustrative worked task follows; authentic manipulatives, ruler data, diagrams, group information gaps and media projects require a teacher-checked learner artifact. Student source: https://im.kendallhunt.com/MS/students/2/4/2/index.html.

KeyConcepts.Rule: A ratio may compare noninteger measures.

KeyConcepts.Rule: Divide the first quantity by the second to find a unit rate.

KeyConcepts.Title: Interpreting evidence
KeyConcepts.Definition: Label and preserve unit order.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Label and preserve unit order.

WorkedExamples.Title: Student-task analogue — Ratios and Rates With Fractions
WorkedExamples.Question: Two runners cover 1.5 km in 3/4 hour and 2.4 km in 1.5 hours respectively. Who has the greater average speed, and what first-party labeled distance–time diagram could show the difference?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use labeled quantities, source-appropriate models and explain which amount represents 100%. Preserve teacher review for open-ended artifacts.
Steps: Plot time (h) horizontally and distance (km) vertically: first has (0,0),(0.75,1.5) and second (0,0),(1.5,2.4).
Label the units, share the interpretation with a partner, and distinguish speed from the total distances.
WorkedExamples.Answer: First runner is faster, 2 km/h versus 1.6 km/h.
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher checks original graph/rate table and interpretable comparison, not just quotient arithmetic.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Comparing unlabeled fraction ratios can reverse the intended unit rate.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the mathematical relationship or reference amount being assessed.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use the stated rate, base and direction of comparison.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Writing an answer without specifying which quantity is 100% or the measurement unit
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A calculation may be numerically right but contextually wrong.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label the reference quantity and units before computing.

SummaryPoints: A ratio may compare noninteger measures.
Divide the first quantity by the second to find a unit rate.
Label and preserve unit order.

WorkedExamples.Title: Student-task analogue — Revisiting Proportional Relationships
WorkedExamples.Question: An invented fabric shop sells 8 feet of cord for $11.20 and accepts fractional-foot cuts. Predict the charge for 30 feet using a per-foot rate and also a direct scale factor.

WorkedExamples.Method: Use labeled quantities, source-appropriate models and explain which amount represents 100%. Preserve teacher review for open-ended artifacts.
